project_type: Cross-screen one-click dialing system with 4 components: Go relay, Tauri v2 desktop, Kotlin Android app, TypeScript browser extension
language: Go (relay), TypeScript/React (PC frontend), Rust (Tauri backend), Kotlin (Android), TypeScript (browser extension)
build_system: Go modules (relay), npm + Cargo via Tauri CLI (PC), Gradle (Android), npm/webpack (browser extension)
test_framework: Go testing (relay), vitest/jest (PC frontend), JUnit (Android), jest (browser extension)
build_command: relay: cd relay && go build -o relay.exe ./cmd/relay; PC: cd pc && npm install && npm run tauri build; Android: cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug; Extension: cd extension && npm install && npm run build
test_command: relay: cd relay && go test ./...; PC: cd pc && npm test; Android: cd android && ./gradlew test; Extension: cd extension && npm test
verification_instructions: 1. relay: go build compiles, go test passes, WebSocket connects on configured port. 2. PC: tauri build compiles, can connect to relay. 3. Android: gradle assembleDebug compiles. 4. Extension: npm run build produces dist/.
setup_instructions: Go 1.25.1 available, Node.js v22 available, Rust 1.92.0 available, Java 25 + Gradle 8.14 available. All pre-installed in sandbox.
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET network mode - full access to package registries. No Android SDK pre-installed (need to install for Kotlin build). No Tauri CLI pre-installed (install via cargo). No physical devices for end-to-end testing.
contribution_requirements: Greenfield project - no existing contribution guidelines. Follow standard practices for each technology.
key_patterns: WebSocket + JSON protocol for all communication. PIN-based grouping (4-digit). 30s heartbeat. ACK-based message reliability. State machine for connection management.
directory_structure: relay/ - Go WebSocket relay server; pc/ - Tauri v2 desktop app; android/ - Kotlin Android app; extension/ - Chrome/Edge MV3 browser extension
